mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -9.1% to -3.4% over four weeks, indicating a sustained recovery trend. This upward momentum will continue linearly over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above the baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved by 5.7 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily increased from 2.3% to 5.7%, signaling growing consumer confidence in essential shopping. This confidence spillover will drive discretionary retail visits upward as consumers resume normal shopping patterns over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 5.7% in t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase week-on-week in at least 3 of the next 4 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 5.0%.

candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -27.7% in t-0w, most negative series
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next two weeks while TRANSIT remains below -20%.

Combined with TRANSIT depression at -27.7%, this dual constraint on commuting will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks as weekday retail footfall remains limited.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain within 1 percentage point of their t-0w values
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -6.7% for t-1w and t-0w
fact:TRANSIT flat at -27.7% for t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean by more than 1 percentage point while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain stalled.

candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15% in the current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -16.4% in t-0w, lowest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week in at least 2 of the next 2 weeks following PARKS decline below -15%.

This normalization of residential patterns, combined with rising GROCERY_PHARM at 5.7%, signals consumer confidence returning. RETAIL_REC will accelerate upward as consumers resume normal mobility routines over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3.5% and GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5.0% simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28-day mean despite both RESIDENTIAL below 3.5% and GROCERY_PHARM above 5.0%.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain in the specified depressed regime.

However, PARKS decline to -16.4% and TRANSIT stagnation at -27.7% will constrain further retail gains. Over one week, the competing forces will stabilize RETAIL_REC near current levels without significant directional change.
